## The complete existence interval {#sec-interval}

Use the full-sided-wait model of @xue-zhong-2026, with $3n$ ranks and
$3m+1$ tiles before drawing. A meld is a triplet or three consecutive ranks.
The physical copy cap $q$ means that each multiplicity $c_i$ satisfies
$c_i+1\le q$ for a live draw. Here the copy cap is allowed to vary.

The [earlier note](live-waits.html) established the exact cap-four interval
and the necessity of at least four physical copies. These combine into a
complete answer for arbitrary natural $q$.

::: {#thm-any-cap}
## Existence at any cap

For natural numbers $n,q,m$, a live full-sided wait exists if and only if

$$
\begin{gathered}
q\ge4,\\
n<m<n(q-1).
\end{gathered}
$$
:::

The inequalities exclude order zero automatically. For every cap $q\ge4$
at positive order $n$, the least possible meld count is $n+1$.

::: {.proof}

Necessity follows from three bounds: every full-sided wait has $m>n$;
some rank contains at least three tiles, so liveness requires $q\ge4$;
and summing $c_i\le q-1$ gives $3m+1\le3n(q-1)$.

For sufficiency, induct on $q-4$. Cap four is the earlier construction.
At a larger cap, if $m<3n$, the same cap-four hand still works.
Otherwise $m\ge3n$ and

$$
n<m-n<n(q-2).
$$

The induction hypothesis supplies a hand at cap $q-1$ with $m-n$ melds.
Add the $n$ disjoint sequences

$$
\begin{gathered}
(1,2,3),\ (4,5,6),\ \ldots,\\
(3n-2,3n-1,3n).
\end{gathered}
$$

Each multiplicity increases by exactly one, and the meld count increases by
$n$. Every old winning decomposition extends by these sequences, while the
new hand respects cap $q$. This proves @thm-any-cap.
:::

::: {#tbl-nine-ranks}

| Copy cap | Possible meld counts for $n=3$ |
|:--------:|:-------------------------------|
| $3$      | None                           |
| $4$      | $4,\ldots,8$                    |
| $5$      | $4,\ldots,11$                   |
| $6$      | $4,\ldots,14$                   |

The exact intervals on nine ranks. These are existence results, rather than
counts of hands.
:::

## A sharp endpoint with an explicit witness {#sec-maximum}

::: {#cor-maximum}
## Largest live meld count

For $n>0$ and $q\ge4$, the largest live meld count is $n(q-1)-1$.
One extremal hand has $q-1$ copies of every rank except for $q-3$ copies
of the penultimate rank:

$$
(\underbrace{q-1,\ldots,q-1}_{3n-2},q-3,q-1).
$$
:::

Start with the cap-four extremal hand and add $q-4$ complete layers.
This gives the displayed multiplicities, preserves every winning draw,
and raises the meld count to $n(q-1)-1$. For example, at $n=3,q=5$ the hand
$(4,4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4)$ attains eleven melds.

## A complement duality on three ranks {#sec-duality}

At order $n=1$, the existence interval $2\le m\le q-2$ is symmetric about
$q/2$. There is also an explicit bijection explaining the symmetry of the
numbers of hands.

For an integer hand $c=(c_1,c_2,c_3)$, let $s$ be the unique rank in
$\{1,2,3\}$ congruent to $\sum_i i c_i$ modulo three. The order-one
characterization in the structural library says that $c$ is a full-sided
wait precisely when it has size $3m+1$, $c_s\ge1$, and $c_i\ge2$ for $i\ne s$.
Liveness adds the upper bound $c_i\le q-1$.

::: {#thm-duality}
## Three-rank complement

For $m\le q$, the map

$$
D_q(c)_i =
\begin{cases}
q-c_i, & i=s,\\
q+1-c_i, & i\ne s
\end{cases}
$$

is a bijection between live full-sided waits at meld counts $m$ and $q-m$,
with the same copy cap $q$. Its inverse is itself.
:::

::: {.proof}

The weighted sum of the constant triple $(q+1,q+1,q+1)$ is divisible by
three. Subtracting $c$ and one additional tile at rank $s$ gives weighted
residue $-s-s=s$ modulo three. Thus $D_q(c)$ has the same distinguished rank
$s$, and applying $D_q$ twice returns $c$.

At $s$, the map reflects the integer interval $[1,q-1]$ into itself;
at the other two ranks it reflects $[2,q-1]$. It therefore preserves the
full-wait lower bounds and the live upper bounds. Finally,

$$
\sum_i D_q(c)_i=3q+2-\sum_i c_i=3(q-m)+1.
$$

The order-one characterization proves the claim in both directions.
:::

For example, at cap $q=5$, $(3,1,3)$ maps to $(3,4,3)$, exchanging meld counts
two and three. Consequently the live-wait counts are equal at $m$ and $q-m$.
This duality concerns three ranks; no higher-order analogue is asserted here.
The [three-rank counting note](three-ranks.html) gives a disjoint box
decomposition and an exact formula for the total number of live hands.

## Checked Lean sources {#sec-lean}

[CapacitySpectrum.lean](CapacitySpectrum.lean) proves the equivalence,
the maximal count, and the coordinates and liveness of the displayed witness.
Its `add_layer` lemma implements the induction step. It imports the two
earlier files [LiveMaximum.lean](LiveMaximum.lean) and
[CopyBound.lean](CopyBound.lean).
[OrderOneDuality.lean](OrderOneDuality.lean) proves the complement's fixed-class
invariance, involutivity, size formula, preservation of liveness, the explicit
equivalence, and the equality of cardinalities.

The sources use Lean 4.35.0 and the structural library at
[this revision](https://github.com/lunaluteus/ninegates-lean4/tree/7b379afe7f54f34c59c8abdfc8e6fa5f0bee952a).
From this SunQuarTeX checkout, run:

```sh
uv run python examples/live-waits/check-lean.py \
  --library /path/to/ninegates-lean4
```

The [checker](check-lean.py) compiles the seven companion modules with strict
linters in a temporary directory, then checks that the twenty-four audited
declarations use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
Rendering the document displays the mathematics; this command separately
checks the proofs. The construction uses no enumeration of candidate hands.
